pageCache.pageTitle: Saltwood Church of England Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Saltwood Church of England Primary School
As the Acting Headteacher I would like to welcome you to our community and invite you to explore the website which I hope will give you an impression of the caring ethos with which we seek to educate the children at both of our schools.
If you are looking for a school place in September 2026, please contact us to book a tour of our friendly school and its extensive grounds!
The Federation of Saltwood and Bodsham Primary Schools is a well established collaboration between two high performing schools with shared Christian Values.
Saltwood Church of England Primary School consistently achieves results above national averages as a result of high standards of teaching, positive attitudes to learning and excellent behaviour from our children.
The school sits at the centre of the village of Saltwood, just outside of Hythe. We have close links with St Peter and St Paul Church nearby and the children have regular opportunities to worship there.
I believe time spent in primary school sets the foundations upon which all future learning is built. We aim to provide a nurturing and creative community, where all children are taught to believe they can make a positive difference to the world.
I look forward to welcoming you.
Mr Martin ThomasActing Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Saltwood Church of England Primary School - PE & Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
PE & Sports Premium
Sport Premium Funding Statement
What is the Sport Premium?
The Government is providing over £320 million a year to improve Physical Education (PE) and Sport in primary schools, to improve healthy lifestyles among pupils and tackle childhood obesity. Saltwood Church of England Primary School is receiving £17,840 for the year 2024-25.
Schools can choose how they use the funding, for example to:
At Saltwood School we have used the Sport Premium to improve the engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity by participating in the Shepway Sports Trust School Games competition package, running extra curricular clubs, allowing children to attend sports events in and out of school such as District Sports.
Saltwood School has also bought into The Shepway School Games Competition Package as well as a variety of sporting workshops provided by the Shepway Sports Trust.
This involves our pupils in a whole range of activities and inter-school competitions from years R-6, including tournaments of Football, Cricket, Reception Fun Days, Handball and Cross Country. This funding provides pupils from years R-6 with opportunities to take part in a variety of both traditional and non-traditional sports. This year workshops and intra-school competitions include Rugby Tots, Tri-Golf, American Football, Hockey and Yoga.
Increased participation in competitive sport.
Healthy lifestyles are promoted.

Curriculum
Our curriculum has been carefully designed to help all our children develop into confident, responsible young people who are ready to take the next steps in their lives. In the context of our Christian values of Love, Creativity and Strength, we have identified eight key attributes we seek to develop in our children through our curriculum.
We have created a curriculum map for each year group which explains how what is taught seeks to develop each of these attributes. Our children receive a broad and rich programme of learning experiences based on the Early Years Foundation Stage in Year R and the National Curriculum in Key Stage 1 and 2.

pageCache.pageTitle: Saltwood Church of England Primary School - Starting School
pageCache.text:
Admission into Reception Class
LOOKING TO START SCHOOL IN SEPTEMBER 2026?
Thank you for considering Saltwood Church of England Primary School for your child. You are making an important decision and we wish to do all we can to support you in this process.
Please contact the school office (details below) to book a tour of our school and its grounds so that you can see how our children learn and play together. Tour dates are available every week until Christmas!
If you decide to apply for a place at our school, please refer to the admissions section of our website for full details.
Once you have secured a place at Saltwood, we have a programme of transition events in the Summer Term to support a smooth and enjoyable start to school life:
HOME VISITS AND NURSERY VISITS
Home visits allow us to meet you and your child in an informal setting and begin our effective partnership. We also visit your child in their nursery setting and each nursery is invited to bring the children to school for an additional visit.
NEW PARENT INDUCTION MEETING AND SCHOOL VISIT
You are invited to attend an induction meeting whilst your child visits their new classroom for an afternoon to play with a small group of current EY children and children who will be in their class.
STORY AND SINGING TIMES
Your child will be invited in to enjoy story and singing times with their new teacher and class.
You are most welcome to join us for Sports Day and our Summer Fete.
If your child is not yet 5 at the beginning of the academic year, we can discuss a more flexible approach to starting school if this is appropriate.
This is held once your child has started school to provide further information.
FRIENDS OF SALTWOOD SCHOOL
An afternoon tea for new parents is held early in the new term where you can meet other parents from our PFA.
We enjoy a close partnership with parents and have an open door policy if you should wish to speak to us at any time. You will be kept updated throughout your child’s time in Early Years by Tapestry, parents’ evenings, stay and play sessions and times to come and share Learning Journey book.
School Office: 01303 266058
Email: enquiries@saltwood.kent.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Saltwood Church of England Primary School - Mrs Lucy Richardson
pageCache.text:
Mrs Lucy Richardson
Saltwood School lost a much loved member of staff with the passing of Lucy Richardson during the summer holiday. She has been described as the caring heart of our school because she dedicated so much of her energy to improving the lives of our children. She was a fantastic class teacher, a highly effective SENCo and a dear friend to us all. Her death came as a huge shock as she continued to work right up to the last day of term. The love felt for Lucy was clear to see as more than 300 people attended her funeral on Wednesday, we are lucky to have the support of such a close-knit community of here at Saltwood.
Lucy's family are asking for donations to be made to Breast Cancer UK. A link to their appeal page can be found here

pageCache.pageTitle: Saltwood Church of England Primary School - Special Educational Needs
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs
Hello my name is Ellie Geering and I am the Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo) at Saltwood Church of England Primary School.
I am in school every day and can be contacted via the school office on:
Phone: 01303 266058 Email: senco@saltwood.kent.sch.uk
At Saltwood Church of England Primary School we strive to support all children to enable them to achieve and meet their full potential. In order to do this, many steps are taken to support them on their learning journeys.
Quality First Teaching is the foundation for all learning experiences. However, for some children there may be occasions where further additional support may be needed to help them to access a full academic and social experience and maximise their learning journey.
How we identify pupils who may require additional support:
One of my main roles is to liaise with staff and parents to monitor and plan further provision, where necessary, and evaluate the impact of these. I meet regularly with a wide range of external agencies including Speech and Language therapists, Specialist teaching and learning service, Educational Psychology, School Nurses, and Early Help. These are all able to offer help, support and specialist advice.
Our school works to support speech, language and communication with support from our NHS link speech & language therapist as well as specialist teachers. I will have regular meetings with our link Speech and Language therapist to discuss our school's provision.
If you have any concerns about your child’s speech, language or communication skills, please speak to your child’s class teacher in the first instance.
If we have discussed a specific concern with you about your child’s speech, language or communication, or you have raised a concern, we will decide together whether to discuss this with our link therapist. You will be kept informed of any plans to support your child.”
Here at Saltwood Church of England Primary School we believe in working as a team, with the child at the heart of every decision we make.
